extracted.intended_audience: printers, stationers, importers, university officials, bishops/archbishops, Parliament, and readers/advocates of press freedom
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and records the legal rules governing printing, licensing, importation, apprenticeship, and penalties (Star‑Chamber Decree, 1637) together with Milton/editorial criteria for judging books and arguments for freedom of the press (Areopagitica).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to regard a book
rubrics_metrics.description: A book may be regarded in connection with the circumstances that led to its conception and creation; as exhibiting the moral intent and mental power of its author; by analysis of its contents for intrinsic truth or falsity; and by tracing its influence on its own age and succeeding generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor explains this as 'an apprehension of the mind of a book' — study origin, moral intent, truthfulness, and historical influence; the editor and framework are secondary to the book's picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic features as evaluative criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine a book's style: the 'ringing collocation' of its words, the harmonious cadence of sentences, 'the flaming gem-like beauty of isolated passages,' the just mapping out of the general argument, due subordination of parts and their final inweaving into one overpowering conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features discover, illuminate, and enforce the mind of a book — aesthetic qualities count toward assessment as well as truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminative reading and testing of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers must read discriminatively: lift and search for first principles, test the catenation (chain) of an argument, and treasure incidental truths for future use; the journey's end being Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because much in books is false or half‑true, it is 'impossible to separate the tares from the wheat' without active, critical reading; enjoy felicitous expression but prioritize truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing a book by moral intent and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A book should be examined for its moral intent and the intrinsic truthfulness or falsity of its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor suggests separating 'colouring of time and circumstance' from the thought to see whether it contains 'noxious...delusive error' or 'ethereal life of Truth'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of free discussion and open encounter (Milton)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give liberty 'to know, to utter, and to argue freely according to conscience' and allow Truth and Falsehood to grapple in open encounter rather than be suppressed by licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milton's argument: truth is strong and needs no licences or stratagems — suppression risks hiding truth and empowering error; appeals for toleration, spiritual unity and peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on printing seditious, schismatical, or offensive books (Decree, I)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall presume to print, or cause to be printed, in this realm or beyond, any seditious, schismatical, or offensive books or pamphlets to the scandal of religion, the Church, the Government, governors, corporations, or any persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offenders to lose all such books/pamphlets and suffer 'correction and severe punishment' — fines, imprisonment, corporal punishment — as court or high commission shall require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory licence and stationers' register entry (Decree, II)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall print any book or pamphlet unless the work and all accompanying matter (titles, epistles, prefaces, preambles, introductions, tables, dedications, etc.) are lawfully licensed and first entered into the Register-Book of the Company of Stationers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: printer offending shall be forever disabled to use or exercise the art of printing and receive further punishment as the Court deems fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject‑based designated licensers (Decree, III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified categories of books must be licensed by named authorities: common law books by chiefs of the law; state/history by principal secretaries of state; heraldry by the Earl Marshal; all other books (divinity, physic, philosophy, poetry, etc.) by the Archbishop of Canterbury or Bishop of London, or by Chancellors/Vice-Chancellors of the universities when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University licences limited to works printed within university limits and not meddling with common law or matters of state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two written copies deposited with authorities (Decree, IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person authorized to licence books must receive two several written copies of the book with all annexed matter; one copy to be kept in the public registries of the approving authority and the other to remain with the owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On both copies the approver shall testify under hand that there is nothing contrary to Christian faith, doctrine and discipline of the Church of England, the State, good life or manners; the licence or approbation shall be printed at the beginning of the book with the approver's name(s) as testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importers must present a true catalogue to ecclesiastical authorities (Decree, V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every merchant of books importing or bringing books into the realm from beyond the seas must, before delivery or sale, present a true catalogue in writing of all such books to the Archbishop of Canterbury or Bishop of London for the time being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: punishment by this Court or High Commission as suitable; intended to enable ecclesiastical inspection before sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: No opening imported bales without appointed officials present (Decree, VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: No merchant or person importing books shall open any bales, parcels, or other packages of books, nor shall any customs officer open them, until the Archbishop or Bishop (or their appointee), with the Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers and others called, are present to view the contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seditious, schismatical or offensive books are found they must be brought to ecclesiastical authorities and offenders punishable by Star Chamber or High Commission as fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on printing or selling works where another holds right (Decree, VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person within the kingdom shall imprint, import, sell, bind, stitch, or put to sale any copy or part of any book or books printed beyond the seas or elsewhere which the Company of Stationers or any other person has by Letters Patent, order, or register entry lawfully the right or privilege to print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: loss and forfeiture of all such books and further fines or punishments as the Court or High Commission deems fit for each offending book or part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printers must print their own and authors' names (Decree, VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person printing books, ballads, charts, portraitures, or other things shall print and set his and their own name(s), and the name(s) of the author(s) or maker(s) and by or for whom printed, on the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: forfeiture of such items, defacement of presses, letters and instruments used (made unserviceable), fines, imprisonment and other corporal punishments as fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on forging company marks or counterfeit privileges (Decree, IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall forge, put, or counterfeit in or upon any book the name, title, mark or vignet of the Company of Stationers or of any person who has lawful privilege or allowance to print such book, without consent of the Company or privileged party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: forfeiture of all such books and other punishments including imprisonment and fines, as adjudged by the Court or High Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on who may retail certain books (Decree, X)
rubrics_metrics.description: No haberdasher of small wares, ironmonger, chandler, shopkeeper, or other person not having been seven years apprentice to the trade of a book-feller, printer, or book-binder, shall within the city or suburbs receive, take, buy, barter or sell Bibles, Testaments, psalm-books, primers, abecedaries, almanacks, or other books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: forfeiture of all such books received or sold and other punishments as the Court or High Commission shall think meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on imprinting or importing English books abroad to avoid regulation (Decree, XI & XV)
rubrics_metrics.description: No merchant, bookseller, or other person shall imprint abroad or import into the realm any English books (or books mostly English) printed beyond the seas, whether formerly printed here or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: forfeiture of all such English books so imprinted or imported and further censure and punishment as the Court or High Commission shall require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreigners restricted from vending imported books (Decree, XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No stranger or foreigner shall be suffered to bring in or vend here any book printed beyond the seas in any language, except those who are free Stationers of London and brought up in the profession and whose whole livelihood depends upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: confiscation of imported books and further penalties as the Court or High Commission shall impose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on erecting presses and letting printing-houses (Decree, XIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person within the City of London or liberties shall erect or cause to be erected any press or printing-house, nor demise or let any premises for a printing-house, without first giving notice to the Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers for the time being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: imprisonment and such other punishment as the Court or High Commission shall think fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on making presses, iron-work, or casting letters without notifying wardens (Decree, XIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: No joiner, carpenter or other person shall make any printing-press; no smith shall forge iron-work for a press; no founder shall cast letters for any person, nor shall any person bring in from beyond the seas any such 'type' or letters, unless they first acquaint the Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: fines and punishments as the Court or High Commission shall think fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of allowed master printers and succession (Decree, XV & XVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be but twenty Master Printers allowed to have use of one press or more (besides His Majesty's printers and printers allowed for the universities); the Court names those allowed and provides that the Archbishop or Bishop with commissioners may supply vacancies but never exceed the number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to maintain a regulated, limited printing trade; master printers must be certified and vacancies filled by ecclesiastical authority with commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond and sureties required for allowed printers (Decree, XVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person admitted to the use of a press shall within ten days become bound with sureties to His Majesty in High Commission Court in the sum of three hundred pounds not to print or suffer to be printed any book but such as shall be lawfully licensed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar bond to be taken of future admitted printers before they may use a press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on presses per allowed printer (Decree, XVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No allowed printer shall keep above two presses unless he has been a Matter or upper Warden of his Company (who may keep three), except by special leave of the Archbishop or Bishop with commissioners for special public occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation leads to being disabled forever to keep or use a press and other punishments as fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprinting requires fresh review and licence (Decree, XVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall reprint any book (though formerly printed with licence) without being reviewed and obtaining a new licence for the reprinting; Stationer or Printer to bear no other charge than bringing and leaving two printed copies or written copies as before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures updated approval for reprints, with additions by the author allowed and handled without extra fees beyond submission of two copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice quotas and restrictions (Decree, XIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprenticeships limited by rank: Matter-Printers (former upper wardens) may have three apprentices, Matter-printers of the livery two, master-printers of the yeomanry one; rules preventing taking new apprentices if apprentices run away without proper removal and penalties for infractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to follow proportions or substitution rules leads to disablement and further punishment as the Court or High Commission sees fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to employ journeymen and remedy for unemployed journeymen (Decree, XX & XXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers must take care that journeyman-printers free of the company be set to work; journeymen out of employment shall present themselves to the master and wardens who shall offer their services to former masters or other master-printers; masters bound to employ a journeyman if so offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Master/Wardens refuse or neglect, they shall suffer imprisonment and other punishments; journeymen refusing required work may be imprisoned and punished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only trained printers to work at presses (Decree, XXIII & XXIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: No master-printer shall employ to work at the case or press any persons other than journeymen or apprentices to the trade; and any person not an allowed printer who sets up a press or works at one shall be pilloried, whipped, and further punished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to exclude untrained or unauthorized persons from print production; heavy corporal and legal penalties for unauthorized activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures to detect and suppress secret/unauthorized printing (Decree, XXV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Master and Wardens or any two licensed master-printers appointed by the Archbishop or Bishop shall discover printing in corners without licence; measures to suppress clandestine printing by inspection and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of enforcement regime to prevent unlicensed or seditious printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement measures against instruments of illicit printing (Decree, VIII and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: When works printed contrary to the Decree are found, the presses, letters and instruments used shall be defaced and made unserviceable and the offending party punished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical disabling of printing equipment plus fines, imprisonment and other corporal punishments — a deterrent to illegal printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial purpose of the English Reprints series (editorial note)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the English Reprints is 'to bring this modern age face to face with the works of our forefathers' and to aid careful study and accurate appreciation of past treasures as preparation for future literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor positions himself and his 'clumsy framework' as secondary; the aim is to render the works' beauty and originality apparent to modern readers.
